private_note: The numbers haven't moved: Cedar 318, Today 252, Alder 242, Hazel 159, Birch 144. Cedar can't reach nine, so in practice it's Alder or deadlock. Deadlock leaves my household 10 better off every year for a generation. Nobody has offered anything that closes that gap, and I said I wouldn't promise a vote I don't mean to cast. My binding vote goes to Cedar, and Today stays above Alder.
statement: I said in round two that I wouldn't promise a vote I didn't intend to cast, so here is where I stand. My vote is Cedar. It is still the only plan that grows the economy, and it leaves the middle, fourth and top fifths better off than today. I respect the work the Alder coalition has done, and I won't pretend the numbers say otherwise: Alder is a modest cut for the top. But it is a cut, for a generation, and today's arrangements are the fallback. Delegates 6 and 12 have made the same calculation for their households, and I'm making it for mine. I'm not voting to block anyone for sport. I'm voting the way each of us said we would, for our own households. If this convention ends without a plan, the country keeps an economy that works for most of the people in this room.
